_instructions.how_to_use: This is a worked example so the repository builds the moment you copy it. Replace it with your own details. Every field here is fake.
_instructions.bullets: Write each bullet as: accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z. Lead with the outcome, not the task. Put a number in most of them.
_instructions.length: One page for under ten years of experience. Cut the oldest role before you shrink the type. The build fails if either document runs to two pages.
_instructions.sections: section_order decides which sections appear and in what order. Remove a name from it and that section is gone from the PDF.
_instructions.ordering: Experience first once you have industry experience. Projects first while you are a student or changing field.
_instructions.separators: Write a plain | between items. The pre-processor typesets it.
_instructions.cover_letter_date: Leave cover_letter.date empty and the letter carries the build date.
_instructions.summary: Optional. Strong experience speaks for itself, so summary is left out of section_order in this example.

resume.summary: Backend engineer working on payment infrastructure, looking for a platform role.

bullets: Rebuilt the settlement pipeline serving 40M transactions a day, cutting end-to-end latency from 900ms to 120ms by replacing per-row lookups with a batched read path.
Designed the idempotency layer shared by 12 services, which removed duplicate charges entirely and reduced support escalations by 71%.
Traced an intermittent data loss affecting 0.3% of refunds to a silent retry in the message consumer, and fixed it by making the consumer commit offsets only after a durable write.
Mentored three junior engineers through their first on-call rotation, after which the team's mean time to acknowledge fell from 22 minutes to 6.
Built the ingestion service in Go that backfilled 4 years of event history, 2.1B rows, without downtime on the live cluster.
Automated the weekly reconciliation report, removing 9 engineer-hours a week of manual spreadsheet work.

projects.name: Ledgerline
bullets: An append-only ledger that keeps double-entry invariants under concurrent writes, verified by a property test suite that runs 50k randomised histories per commit.
Chose serializable isolation over application-level locking, because a ledger that is merely fast but occasionally wrong is worth nothing.

projects.name: Quietlog
bullets: Collapses repetitive log lines into counted patterns, which cut one team's log storage bill by 64% with no loss of signal in incident review.

skills.items: Property testing, Distributed tracing, Incident review

publications.citation: R. Chen. Batched settlement without losing serializability. SIGMOD Industrial Track, 2025.

cover_letter.subject: Application for Platform Engineer, REQ-4471
paragraphs: I am applying for the Platform Engineer role. I work on payment infrastructure, most recently a settlement pipeline handling 40M transactions a day which brought end-to-end latency down from 900ms to 120ms, and I would like to do that work on your platform team.

The work closest to yours is Ledgerline. Keeping double-entry invariants true under concurrent writes is the hard part, because the failure is silent and shows up in an audit months later. I made the ledger append-only and serializable, then verified it with 50k randomised histories on every commit. Your job posting describes the same problem at a larger scale.
I also care about the operational side. After I rewrote our on-call runbooks and mentored three engineers through their first rotation, mean time to acknowledge fell from 22 minutes to 6.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how you keep reconciliation correct as volume grows. Thank you for your time.
